holidays.name: National Cocoa Day
holidays.description: A day for mugs of hot chocolate. Think marshmallows, whipped cream, peppermint sticks, and a blanket. Winter has an official excuse to get cozy and a little sugar-buzzed.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance, and its origin is unclear. It has become a fixture of the winter holiday calendar, and it falls in the middle of the season's cold snaps.
holidays.funFact: The Maya and Aztecs drank cacao as a bitter, frothy, often spicy beverage. Sweetened hot chocolate only became popular after cacao reached Europe and people started adding sugar.

holidays.name: National Violin Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the violin, the instrument that can sound like a sob, a bird, or a lightning storm. Listen to a concerto, dust off an old fiddle, or try some scratchy beginner screeches.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. Music lovers and string players use it to honor one of the most expressive instruments in the orchestra.
holidays.funFact: The violin family took its modern form in 16th-century Italy. Instruments made by Antonio Stradivari in the 17th and 18th centuries now sell for millions of dollars.

holidays.name: National Day of the Horse
holidays.description: A day to appreciate horses, the animals that have carried people, pulled plows, and starred in countless movies. Give a favorite horse a carrot, or just admire one from a respectful distance.
holidays.origin: The observance began in the United States as a way to recognize the horse's role in the country's history, economy, and culture. It is a long-running annual tradition on December 13.
holidays.funFact: Horses can sleep standing up. They lock their leg joints, which lets them doze without falling over.
